## Natural history notes

A native peat moss characterized by dense, upright shoots with tightly clustered branch leaves that give the plant a somewhat bristly or hedgehog-like appearance. Hedgehog Sphagnum grows in acidic, waterlogged habitats such as bogs, wet pine flatwoods, seepage areas, and swamp margins, where it can form soft mats or hummocks over saturated soils. Like other Sphagnum mosses, it can hold large amounts of water and helps create and maintain acidic, nutrient-poor wetland conditions. Its growth also contributes to peat accumulation and provides important microhabitat for small invertebrates, microorganisms, and other moisture-dependent species.
